title: Wood screw
prompt: A labelled teaching model of the page 64 wood screw seats a screwdriver in the screw head above one wood specimen. Drive rotates the screw and advances it into the wood as its helical thread engages the material. Reverse turns and withdraws the screw along the same thread path. Test pull applies a modest external axial load to the inserted screw and shows the thread resisting through contact and friction. See-through exposes the head slot, shank, thread, point and surrounding wood contact. Force arrows are overlays. Any fresh wood specimen is an external reset. Do not add a two-board clamping claim or self-repairing wood.
blurb: An enlarged teaching model turns one wood screw into a specimen and reveals how its integral thread engages the wood.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Screws
adaptations: Enlarged and slowed teaching model, not a literal reproduction.
One externally restrained wood specimen; hand torque and axial pull are external inputs.
Force arrows and retained thread-path marks are overlays.
Fresh specimen is an external replacement; removal never repairs wood.
Pull resistance is qualitative, without a strength rating.
telemetry: No production telemetry in this standalone static figure. Local verification only.
